title: Ephemeral prefix bundler and microbatch dedupe for tail-latency reduction
creator: Ava Chen
description: Customers with conversational workloads are seeing spiky tail latencies when many short, similar prefixes hit the GPU KV cache concurrently. Current continuous batching groups by request arrival time but does not opportunistically merge short-lived prefixes that are highly similar across requests, which causes redundant KV slots and memory pressure. This ticket implements an ephemeral prefix bundler that groups and deduplicates compatible prefixes within the microbatch window to reduce GPU KV occupancy and improve 95th/99th latency under bursty load.
acceptance_criteria: Bundler runs inside the existing continuous batching pipeline without increasing median latency by >5% at baseline QPS
95th percentile latency reduced by at least 15% under our conversational microburst replay (existing test harness)
GPU KV memory utilization reduced by >= 20% for representative short-prefix workloads in perf lab runs
No regression on correctness: outputs identical (bit-for-bit or within acceptable token-level variance) compared to baseline when bundler is disabled
Feature toggled by config flag and covered by unit + integration tests and a perf dashboard chart
technical_notes: Design: insert bundler after request normalization and before KV lookup. Each incoming request receives a prefix fingerprint and a short structural signature (token-length, template-id, normalized slot map).
Bundling policy: in microbatch window, group prefixes with identical structural signature and fingerprint Hamming distance <= 2 (on SHA-256-derived 64-bit sketch).
Memory model: allocate ephemeral 'bundled view' KV entries that point to canonical GPU-resident fragments. Canonicalization uses a canonical-key table sharded by GPU slot to avoid cross-GPU locks.
Eviction: ephemeral bundles have TTL tied to microbatch lifecycle; canonicalized fragments participate in existing slab allocator and are reference-counted by bundle handles.
Fallback: if a request has side-channel signals (e.g., per-request CUDA stream affinity or strict real-time flag), skip bundling to preserve tail-latency isolation.
Prefetch optimization: speculative warmup of canonical fragments for bundles with high reuse probability using low-priority prefetch queue to hide copying latency.
Consistency: use compare-and-swap on canonical-key table to dedupe racey inserts. Maintain linearizable visibility within the microbatch window.
Metrics: add per-batch bundle_rate, dedupe_ratio, ephemeral_fragments_created, and canonical_lookup_latency.
Safety: all bundler code is feature-flagged and runs on a per-model config; disabled by default for older model variants and enabled via runtime-1.20 rollout for Canary tenants.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): implement prototype bundler in integration test harness; create synthetic microburst workload that exercises short similar prefixes.
Core impl (5d): add fingerprint/signature extraction, canonical-key table, and bundle grouping logic in batching service layer.
GPU glue (3d): modify KV lookup to accept bundled views and to resolve canonical fragment handles without extra copies where possible.
Eviction & refcounting (2d): wire into slab allocator and validate no leaks with stress harness.
Perf runs & dashboards (2d): run lab experiments, collect metrics, and build dashboard panels for bundle_rate/dedupe_ratio/95th latency.
Canary rollout (3d): enable for subset of tenants, monitor for correctness and latency regressions, iterate based on telemetry.
Docs & tests (2d): add design doc, operational runbook and tests that cover race cases and fallback paths.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike complete — prototype shows ~22% reduction in canonical KV slots on synthetic traffic with 80% similar prefixes. Initial prototype implemented as off-path simulation.
2025-02-18: Implemented fingerprint + signature extractor; integration tests for signature collisions added. Observed negligible collision rate on production-like tokenizer samples.

2025-02-24: Core bundler integrated into batching service; added feature flag and per-batch metrics. Early perf run shows 12% improvement at 95th under default microburst harness; still tuning grouping threshold.
2025-02-27: GPU glue work started — resolved a stale refcount bug; added CAS-based insert to canonical-key table to avoid duplicates under concurrency.
comments: Priya Kapoor (PM): please ensure canary rollout targets both Hosted and Dedicated to validate multi-tenant interaction.
Santiago Ruiz (Infra): watch out for increased kernel launch variance if prefetch is overaggressive — suggested low-priority CUDA stream for prefetch.
Design review (2025-02-20): agreed on signature+fingerprint approach; requested simulation data for collision safety before enabling by default.
notes: This approach favors transient dedupe inside the batching window (ephemeral bundles) rather than global compaction to avoid long-lived canonical fragments for low-reuse prefixes. If successful, follow-up work will evaluate cross-batch canonicalization to further amortize cost.
